title: Flat scalar restriction and the normalized direct-image strict-limit square
statement:
Let $u:\mathscr U\to\mathscr V$ be a geometric morphism of topoi presented by small sites, meaning $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with finite-limit-preserving inverse image [def-weil-pbc-ringed-topos-morphism]. For $T=U,V$ let $a_T:R_T\to S_T$ be a map of sheaves of commutative rings, with $S_T$ flat over $R_T$ (extension of scalars is exact). Fix isomorphisms $u^{-1}R_V\cong R_U$, $u^{-1}S_V\cong S_U$ commuting with $a_T$. Use unbounded derived module categories, obtained by localizing cochain complexes at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and derived strict diagrams with $J=\mathbf N_{\geq1}^{op}$ [lem-weil-pbc-diagram-site-realization]. Write $r_T$ for restriction of scalars, on modules or diagrams [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], $R_u^R,R_u^S$ for ambient derived direct image, and $\mathscr R_u^R,\mathscr R_u^S$ for derived termwise direct image. Let $\chi_u:r_VR_u^S\cong R_u^Rr_U$ and $d_u:r_V\mathscr R_u^S\cong\mathscr R_u^Rr_U$ be exactly the flat scalar comparisons [lem-weil-pbc-flat-ringed-diagram-restriction]. Put $\mathcal L_T^R=R\lim$, $\mathcal L_T^S=R\lim$ on strict diagrams, computed by a K-injective tower resolution followed by ordinary inverse limit; K-injective means that every map from an acyclic complex is null-homotopic. Let $\kappa_u^R,\kappa_u^S$ denote the canonical direct-image/limit comparisons induced by $u_*\lim=\lim u_*^{J}$ [lem-weil-ringed-tower-pushforward-limit-comparison].

For every $Z\in D(\operatorname{Fun}(J,\operatorname{Mod}(S_U)))$, and analogously at $V$, there is a natural isomorphism $\lambda_Z:r_U\mathcal L_U^SZ\cong\mathcal L_U^Rr_UZ$. Its specified ordinary comparison sends a compatible family to that same family, and its derived comparison on a K-injective tower is that ordinary comparison conjugated by the universal total-derived units. With these normalizations one has
$$\mathcal L_V^R(d_{u,Z})\lambda_{\mathscr R_u^SZ}\,r_V(\kappa_u^S(Z))=\kappa_u^R(r_UZ)R_u^R(\lambda_Z)\chi_{u,\mathcal L_U^SZ}.$$
This equality is natural in every derived strict tower $Z$, with no finite-reduction or completeness condition.

proof.text: For an ordinary scalar square F' s isomorphic to r F, form natural units a = qs inverse followed by sD of the first derived unit, and b = Q of the ordinary comparison followed by the second unit followed by the derived image of qr inverse. Both are invertible on K-injectives because r preserves them. Naturality of a implies that the common ordinary functor inverts quasi-isomorphisms between K-injectives. Mathlib LocalizerMorphism.Derives.isRightDerivedFunctor_of_isIso makes both candidate functors universal right derived functors. Functor.rightDerivedUnique supplies the comparison, and rightDerivedNatTrans_app gives a followed by the comparison equals b on every complex. Cancelling qs inverse and qr inverse yields exactly the required normalization. Apply this to ordinary inverse limit at U and V. This also proves the normalization on every complex, which avoids any K-injective preservation requirement on the direct image.

proof.text: For any ordinary tower T compare the two composites into the R_V limit by each limit projection. The projections of limit.post are the scalar or direct-image images of the original projections. The levelwise equation ordinaryd identifies the component of d with chi at T(n). Naturality of chi at the projection T to T(n) identifies the two resulting maps, and limit.hom_ext proves the ordinary square. Apply this equality degreewise to a tower complex.

proof.text: On a K-injective tower I let C = lim I and it = restricted I. The exact constant-tower left adjoint makes C K-injective; flat restriction makes it K-injective. Precompose both derived-square composites with rV of the composite LSU/FS universal unit, an isomorphism, and postcompose with LRV(TR(qtU.hom at I)), also an isomorphism. For the left side use the kappaS normalization, naturality of lambdaV at the TS unit, the d normalization, and the all-complex lambdaV normalization. Naturality of qV and of the LRV unit reduces it to qV at FS(C), followed by Q(sV(cs) then lv then lim(dd)), followed by the common LRV/TR unit. For the right side use naturality of kappaR at qtU, naturality of chi at the LSU unit, the lambdaU normalization, the chi normalization at C, naturality of the FR unit at lu, and the kappaR normalization at it. This gives the same outer factors around Q(chi(C) then FR(lu) then cr). The degreewise ordinary square identifies these two middle maps. Cancel the pre- and postcomposition isomorphisms. The calculation is the private square_of_normalized API lemma for the comparison structures over arbitrary abelian categories; the public theorem specializes it to the concrete module sheaves, avoiding repeated reduction of sheaf and chosen-limit data.

proof.text: Package the two composites as natural transformations on the derived tower category. For any Z choose its localization representative and a K-injective resolution I. The resulting isomorphism Z to QI and naturality transport their equality from QI to Z. Hence the square holds on every derived tower, without exact products, completeness, or finite reduction.
